tiles.title: Filtering Rows with WHERE and Logical Operators

steps.visual_purpose: A small orders table before and after WHERE, with the kept and discarded rows visibly different.
The same three conditions evaluated with and without parentheses, showing which orders are kept in each version.
An orders table with some blank delivery times, showing = NULL returning no rows while IS NULL returns the blank ones.
An unsorted result next to the same rows sorted by one column and then by a tiebreaker, with tied rows highlighted.
A sorted list with the first rows skipped by OFFSET and the next rows kept by LIMIT, shown as a window over the list.
A small column of values collapsing into single summary numbers (count, sum, average, minimum, maximum), with a NULL visibly skipped.
Rows split into per-category buckets, each bucket collapsing into one output row with its own aggregate.
A pipeline showing WHERE filtering raw rows, GROUP BY forming groups, then HAVING filtering the groups.
A CASE expression with its WHEN branches numbered in the order they are tested, beside sample rows and the label each one receives.
The same query shown messy and then reformatted, with the right-aligned keywords and line breaks visible.
Messy city values on the left and their cleaned forms on the right after trimming and case conversion.
A date value with the pulled-out year/month/hour parts and a subtraction of two dates giving a number of days.
The two cast syntaxes side by side producing the same converted value.
A column with blank cells and the same column after COALESCE fills them with a default.
Two result lists stacked into one, with the duplicate row kept by UNION ALL and collapsed by UNION.
Two tables connected on a shared key, with matched rows linked and unmatched rows from either side visibly dropped.
An ON clause with two equality tests joined by AND, next to the equivalent USING (a, b) form.
Two tables joined with unmatched left rows kept and NULL-filled, contrasted with the inner join that drops them.

tiles.title: Query Execution Order and Subqueries in WHERE

steps.visual_purpose: The six processing steps in order (FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT, ORDER BY) mapped onto one running query.
An outer query with a parenthesized inner query inside its WHERE, the inner part highlighted as producing one value or a list.

tiles.title: Subqueries in FROM and Common Table Expressions

steps.visual_purpose: A subquery in FROM with the parentheses, alias and inner column names visibly passed to the outer SELECT and WHERE.
A WITH block above the main query, and the main query reading from the named result as if it were a table.
